column1: # The icons of the house, as measures. `script/icon.py` draws every
# svg in `asset/icon` that has rows here from these rows alone: the svg
# files are what comes out, this file is what is true.
# One construction for all of them, the one the Phi fonts are made on:
# a stroke of one width with round ends, led from point to point, and
# at each point a corner as round as its radius says. What makes one
# icon another is the radius: a speech mark is the frame with one tight
# corner, a house the frame with a round head, a globe the frame fully
# round. A letter is drawn the same way and still reads as its letter.
#   run   an open stroke: points `x y r`, apart by commas; r is how
#         round the corner at that point is (the ends have none)
#   ring  a closed stroke: the same, every point a corner
#   fill  a closed shape, filled: the same
#   pill  a filled pill: `x y wide high`, its ends fully round
#   cut   a closed shape taken out of the fill before it: the same
#   hole  a pill taken out of the fill before it: `x y wide high`
# The table is in three files, read as one: this one, `icon-tool.tsv`
# (what the older apps and Phigen name) and `icon-letter.tsv` (letters,
# Everything is on a square of 24. The frame most icons share is the
# One family of corners (the user, 25 November 2026: every icon of one
# family, in radius and in how its pieces join): a corner is a small
# corner, a corner, or the frame's, the pin's three; a radius from round
# up is an arc, as round as its sides let it be. `script/icon.py` draws
# every corner at the one of these nearest the radius written.
# --- the rail and the menu beside it
# Rooms: the frame with one tight corner, a speech mark; two lines said.
# Hosts, the network: the frame fully round, a meridian and the line
# Shops: a bag, rounder at its foot than at its mouth, and its handle.
# Things: a box, its lid and its label.
# The menu: four cells, one of them fully round.
# Start: a house, the frame with a round head, and its door.
# One person: a head and shoulders.
# People: two heads, two pairs of shoulders.
# A text room: two strokes down, two across.
# A voice room: a speaker and what comes out of it.
# --- a room's tools, a message's controls, the field, the window
# Find: a round glass and its handle.
# Shut, put down, make large: the window's three.
# The one before, the one after.
# Keep at the top: a head, its bar, its needle. Off: struck through.
# A favourite: five points, each a little round.
# Answer: back, and round the corner.
# Liked: two round heads and a point.
# A hand, its thumb up, and its cuff.
# Fire: a drop with its pill.
# A picture: its frame, a sun, a hill. To post one: a smaller frame
# Say it: a dart and its fold.
# Hand on: three ends and what joins them.
# Take: down into a tray. Open elsewhere: out of a frame.
# Speak: a pill, its cradle, its stand. Off: struck through.
# Be seen: a camera's box and its eye.
# Call: a hand's phone and its pill. End it: struck through.
# Hear nothing: the speaker, crossed. Tell me nothing: a bell, struck.
# --- people, coming and going, what is owned
# Light: a round sun and its eight rays. Dark: a disc with the round
# bite the night takes out of it. Glass: two panes, one over the other.
# --- made marks: a filled body and what is cut out of it
# The ones that pointed, found, handed on and starred as line work of
# another house are made as the letters are: a body with round and
# tight corners, a pill taken out where there is something to see.
# Find: a round body, the pill it looks through, and its handle.
# The one before, the one after, up, down: a pill that ends in a head.
# Words on a picture: the square's frame, and the T of the font set in
# it, a bar over a stem.
# Answer: a head, and a pill that comes round the corner to it.
# Hand on: three round ends and the pills that join them.
# A favourite: five round points and the pill in its middle.
# --- the pin of the bar's menu
# The frame and a pill in it: wide while the menu is shown, narrow
# while it is put away. Open and shut differ in the pill alone.
# A robot: a head with its screen's pill, a body under it.
# A leaf: round on one side, a tight point at its tip, and its vein.
# --- the botanist's mark: Phiber's square, every corner round: 10 at
# top-right and bottom-left, 4 at top-left and bottom-right; and two bars
# cut in it, the pair in the middle of the square, each a pill softened at
# two opposite corners as Phiogy's long bar is, the short one half the long
# one's height and two thirds its width, two apart and a point lower.
# A list: three lines, a dot before each.
